data.answer: Everything Legendary, a Black-owned vegan burger brand, has rapidly expanded its retail presence, growing from a family kitchen operation to being sold in 1,500 grocery stores including Target, Safeway, and Publix. The company raised $6 million to support its growth, aiming to disrupt the multi-billion-dollar plant-based food market with its unique blend of hemp protein, coconut oil, potato starch, and beet extract. It plans to expand to 5,600 grocery stores and has announced an expansion to 1,000 Target locations nationwide.

results.content:
“There are a lot of people trying to get into the $5 billion-plus plant-based food market,” said Duane “Myko” Cheers, co-founder of Everything Legendary. “What has our investors excited about us is they can see that we aren’t just another plant-based product ... we are looking to disrupt the multi-billion-dollar industry with unprecedented flavor, premium ingredients and high-energy marketing that sets our brand apart. Having partners like CircleUp and General Mills, that work with some of the biggest brands in the world, is an amazing honor.”

The funding will support the company’s retail expansion, new product development and field marketing activities. Products on tap include plant-based sausage, boneless wings and breakfast patties.

# How This Black-Owned Vegan Burger Brand Nearly Quadrupled Its Reach in One Year

## In less than a year, Black-owned vegan company Everything Legendary has grown from a family kitchen operation to a brand with a national retail footprint and a new $6 million capital infusion.

by
Nicole Axworthy

February 14, 2022 [...] Founded in 2019 by Duane “Myko” Cheers, Danita Claytor, and Chef Jumoke Jackson, Everything Legendary’s rapid growth began in early 2021 when they were hand-making burgers in their own kitchen and shipping them directly to customers. The trio’s unique vegan burgers are made from a proprietary blend of hemp protein, coconut oil, potato starch, and beet extract. In just 10 months, they went from zero to 1,500 grocery stores including Safeway, Acme, Giant, Target, Ralphs, Kings, and Balduccis, with additional placements coming in Sprouts, Meijer, Publix, and more in the coming months.

From an episode of Shark Tank to the aisles of Target, Everything Legendary is making a splash in the plant-based sector. Recently, its impact got a little bit bigger as it announced it will be expanding its presence in 1,000 Target locations nationwide, making it one of the largest Black-owned, plant-based meat manufacturers sold at the big-box chain.

Duane Cheers, Co-Founder, Everything Legendary"In 2021, we went from a $300,000 Shark Tank deal to a nationwide presence in Target stores with 310 locations in 13 states," said Duane Cheers, Co-Founder of Everything Legendary. "Today, the number of store locations has more than tripled due to Target's commitment to investing in Black-owned businesses."
